correctness.rationale: Parseval applied to the square of the polynomial and equality in each complex triangle inequality give exactly the equal-two-square relations, since all ordered-pair magnitudes are positive. Modulo 16 the unordered pairs of classes 0 mod 4, 2 mod 4, and odd have disjoint squared-sum residue sets. Modulo 3 the count of nonmultiples of 3 is fixed. Modulo 5 the sole ambiguity among unordered pairs of square residues is {0,0} versus {1,4}, both with character sum zero. The matrix of the resulting six features on indices 1–6 has determinant 120 (independently computed by the signed permutation formula). Independent grouping of unordered pairs with repetition found exactly the collisions 50, 65, 85 at N=10 and additionally 125, 130 at N=11. They solve with unit pivots for 7,8,9,11,10. For k≥12 take the representative a of 3k mod 5 in {1,...,5}, then ((3k+4a)/5,(4k−3a)/5) is integral, positive, and strictly below k in each coordinate. The orthogonal identity replaces k by earlier indices with unit pivot. Thus the full torus is the graph over the first six phases, without extra torsion components; the determinant is the degree of the specific parameter map. The N=10 group instead has seven free coordinates.
